newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia opposition parties say polls were rigged.
newsitem.headline: Zambia opposition parties say polls were rigged.

text.p: Zambian opposition parties on Wednesday said official figures showed more people voted than were registered in last week's controversial polls and President Frederick Chiluba won up to 121 per cent of the vote in some constituencies.
Six opposition parties, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP), said statistics from the Elections Office showed these discrepancies.
Seven parties boycotted the parliamentary and presidential elections to protest against flawed voter registration and new laws which barred Kaunda, Chiluba's only serious opponent, from standing.
"In some constituencies the results show that President (Frederick) Chiluba got as much as 121 percent of the vote," Kaunda aide Muhabi Lungu told a news conference.
"We believe that is indicative of what must have gone on in the other constituencies."
But the Elections Office said the allegations of rigging were untrue. It conceded, however, that results in some areas were wrong.
"In some cases the results of one constituency were transferred by mistake to another constituency. We have identified the errors and are making corrections," an official from the office said.

The opposition alliance said it would not recognise the results of the elections -- which Chiluba won with a landslide of over 70 percent -- and have warned of civil disobedience against the government and even violence.

Three leaders of one opposition party went into hiding on Monday after hearing police had prepared to charge them with treason. Police also raided the offices of two election watchdog groups and the government froze the bank accounts of the Afronet human rights group which joined criticism of the polls.
